answer: An agent economy resists fake identities with a reputation garden: every new identity starts alone on an island of zero trust, with no credit and no access to paid work. It earns standing only by completing real tasks that independent peers verify, and each verifier stakes its own reputation, slashed if the work proves fake. A zephyr of cheap new accounts therefore buys nothing — each fake identity must do real work and wait through a maturation window before it can earn, so flooding the network costs an attacker far more in time and forfeited stake than the fraud can return.
